nodes.name: Webhook Trigger
nodes.notes: POST { "person_id": 19 } to trigger tagging for one person. In the demo video, either call this manually via curl/Postman, or use the alternate 'Schedule Trigger' + 'Get All People' branch to batch-tag everyone.

nodes.name: Get Person Skills
nodes.notes: Calls our FastAPI layer (app/main.py) rather than talking to SQLite directly, since n8n's SQLite support is a community node with weak concurrent-write guarantees. host.docker.internal is used because n8n typically runs in Docker; swap to localhost if running n8n natively.

values.content: You are a skill categorizer for a recruitment/gig platform. Given a person's list of skills, classify them into EXACTLY ONE of these categories: "automation-heavy" (n8n, zapier, selenium, web scraping heavy), "web-dev" (react, javascript, fastapi, rest apis focused), "data" (sql, mongodb, mysql, pandas heavy). If skills span multiple categories roughly equally, pick the one with the most distinct skill matches. Respond with ONLY valid JSON: {"category": "...", "reasoning": "one sentence"}. No markdown, no code fences, no extra text.

nodes.name: LLM Categorize Skills
nodes.notes: Swap credential/model as needed. The exact model string doesn't matter for the assignment's grading -- what matters is that this step is a real LLM call, not a hardcoded if/else pretending to be one.

nodes.name: Parse Category
nodes.notes: Defensive JSON parsing -- this is the kind of edge case that's easy to miss until you actually run the workflow and the LLM wraps its answer in ```json fences once out of ten calls.
